newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Prominent pro-Beijing politician in HK dies.
newsitem.headline: Prominent pro-Beijing politician in HK dies.

text.p: A prominent pro-China politician in Hong Kong, Liu Yiu-chu, died on Sunday aged 63 after a long illness, a hospital spokeswoman said.

Liu, a local delegate to the Chinese parliament, the National People's Congress, criticised both China and Britain on arrangements for the handover of sovereignty of Hong Kong, which will return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
She opposed China's plan to install a provisional assembly that will dismantle democratic reforms that British Governor Chris Patten introduced in the twilight of colonial rule.
Liu said the provisional legislature, chosen by a China-assembled caucus, was illegal under the Basic Law, the territory's post-colonial constitution.
But Liu was equally vociferous in assailing Patten's reforms, which she said were a breach of the post-1997 constitution.
The pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong also condemns the interim assembly, saying it lacks a legal basis.
